title: Medicare Scam Calls Threaten to Cancel Benefits
how_it_works: Scammers call pretending to be from Medicare. They say your benefits will be canceled unless you give them personal information or pay a fee. They may sound urgent and try to scare you.
example_message: "This is Medicare. We need to confirm your Social Security number or your benefits will be suspended immediately."
red_flags: Caller asks for your Social Security number or bank info
what_to_do: Hang up and call Medicare directly at 1-800-MEDICARE if you have questions.

title: Fake Tech Support Pop-Up on Your Computer
how_it_works: A pop-up appears on your computer saying you have a virus. It tells you to call a number for help. If you call, scammers may ask for remote access to your computer or ask for payment.
example_message: "Warning! Your computer is infected. Call Microsoft Support now at 1-888-123-4567."
red_flags: Unsolicited pop-up warning about a virus
Asked to call a number right away
Asked to pay for tech support or give remote access
what_to_do: Close the pop-up and do not call the number. If you need help, contact a trusted local computer expert.

title: Grandparent Emergency Scam
how_it_works: Someone calls pretending to be your grandchild or a police officer. They say your grandchild is in trouble and needs money right away. They ask you not to tell anyone.
example_message: "Grandma, it’s me! I’m in jail and need bail money. Please send $2,000 and don’t tell mom and dad."
red_flags: Caller claims to be a relative in trouble
Requests money urgently, often by wire transfer or gift cards
what_to_do: Hang up and call your grandchild or another family member to check the story.

title: Social Security Text Message Scam
how_it_works: You get a text saying there’s a problem with your Social Security account. The message tells you to click a link or call a number. Scammers want your personal information.
example_message: "Your Social Security account is locked. Click here to unlock it: [fake link]"
red_flags: Message urges you to click a link or call a number
what_to_do: Do not click any links or reply. Delete the message.

title: Romance Scam on Social Media
how_it_works: A scammer pretends to be interested in a relationship online. After gaining your trust, they ask for money for an emergency or travel. They often avoid meeting in person.
example_message: "I care about you so much, but I need your help. Can you send me $500 for a plane ticket to visit you?"
red_flags: Person you’ve never met asks for money
Refuses to meet in person or video chat
Stories about emergencies or needing money quickly
what_to_do: Never send money to someone you haven’t met in person.
